fr: QVCT (qualité de vie et des conditions de travail)
def: The overall conditions in which people work and how they experience them, covering workload, work organisation, relationships, the working environment and the balance with personal life.

formal.uk: quality of working life and working conditions
formal.us: quality of work life and working conditions
formal.ex: The parties have agreed to open negotiations on [[quality of working life and working conditions]] in the first quarter.
formal.ex_us: The parties have agreed to open negotiations on [[quality of work life and working conditions]] in the first quarter.

everyday.ex: Our [[quality of working life]] scores dropped sharply after the move to the new site.
everyday.ex_us: Our [[quality of work life]] scores dropped sharply after the move to the new site.

collocations: to improve the quality of working life
a quality of working life survey
note_fr: « QVCT » n'est pas un sigle connu à l'étranger : développez-le ou parlez de « wellbeing and working conditions ». La notion française (ex-QVT) est plus large que le « wellbeing » anglo-saxon : elle inclut l'organisation du travail, la charge et le dialogue social.

explain.written: QVCT (qualité de vie et des conditions de travail) is a French concept covering employees' working conditions, work organisation, workload and work-life balance, on which employers with union representation are required to negotiate periodically.
explain.spoken: QVCT is the French umbrella term for quality of working life - wellbeing, yes, but also how work is organised and how much people have on their plate.

term.uk: agreement on quality of working life
term.us: agreement on quality of work life

def: A company-level collective agreement setting out the measures an employer will take on working conditions, work organisation and work-life balance.

formal.uk: agreement on quality of working life
formal.us: agreement on quality of work life
formal.ex: The [[agreement on quality of working life]] was concluded for a period of three years.
formal.ex_us: The [[agreement on quality of work life]] was concluded for a period of three years.

everyday.ex: We signed a [[wellbeing agreement]] with the unions two years ago, and it's up for renewal.
everyday.ex_us: We signed a [[well-being agreement]] with the unions two years ago, and it's up for renewal.

collocations: the monitoring committee of the agreement
note_fr: En France, la QVCT fait partie d'un bloc de négociation obligatoire périodique (avec l'égalité professionnelle) dans les entreprises où existent des sections syndicales représentatives. Au Royaume-Uni et aux États-Unis, ces sujets relèvent en général de politiques internes décidées par l'employeur, pas d'accords.

explain.written: An accord QVCT is a French collective agreement, negotiated with the unions, on working conditions, work organisation and work-life balance; this subject forms part of the periodic negotiations required by law.
explain.spoken: It's an agreement we negotiate with the unions on wellbeing and working conditions - things like workload, remote work and the right to disconnect.

def: The degree to which people can meet the demands of their job while keeping enough time and energy for their personal and family life.

formal.uk: balance between professional and private life
formal.us: balance between professional and private life
formal.ex: The Company is committed to promoting a healthy [[balance between professional and private life]].

everyday.ex: Most people who leave us mention [[work-life balance]] in their exit interview.

informal.ex: People want a decent salary, but they also want [[a life outside work]].

collocations: to strike a better work-life balance
note_fr: On dit simplement « work-life balance », sans « personal ». « Private life » est formel et peut évoquer la vie privée au sens juridique. Le verbe usuel : « to strike a balance » (trouver un équilibre).

def: To stop thinking about work and relax properly when you are not working.

formal.ex: Managers should allow employees [[to disconnect from work]] outside their normal working hours.

everyday.ex: I find it really hard [[to switch off]] when my laptop's on the kitchen table.

informal.ex: Everyone needs [[to unplug]] properly over the summer.

collocations: to be unable to switch off
note_fr: « Se déconnecter » au sens psychologique = « to switch off » ou « to unwind ». « To disconnect » existe mais sonne technique ; le droit à la déconnexion se dit « right to disconnect ».

def: To feel that your work and your contribution are noticed and appreciated by your employer and colleagues.

formal.uk: to feel that one's contribution is recognised
formal.us: to feel that one's contribution is recognized
formal.ex: Employees need [[to feel that their contribution is recognised]].
formal.ex_us: Employees need [[to feel that their contribution is recognized]].

everyday.ex: People don't leave because of pay alone; they leave because they don't [[feel valued]].

informal.ex: A quick thank-you goes a long way - people just want [[to feel appreciated]].

note_fr: « Valorisé » ne se traduit pas par « valorised » (inexistant dans ce sens). Le contraire : « to feel undervalued » ou « to feel taken for granted » (avoir l'impression qu'on vous doit tout).

def: To feel that your opinions have been listened to and taken seriously.

formal.uk: to feel that one's views are taken into account
formal.us: to feel that one's views are taken into account
formal.ex: Staff must [[feel that their views are taken into account]] if the consultation is to mean anything.

everyday.ex: The survey only works if people [[feel heard]] at the end of it.

note_fr: « Se sentir écouté » : « to feel heard » ou « to feel listened to ». Oublier le « to » final (« to feel listened ») est une faute fréquente.

def: The feeling of being accepted and of being an integral part of a team or an organisation.

formal.ex: Our team rituals are designed to strengthen employees' [[sense of belonging]] across all sites.

everyday.uk: to feel part of the team
everyday.us: to feel part of the team
everyday.ex: New joiners who work mostly from home don't always [[feel part of the team]].

collocations: to foster a sense of belonging
note_fr: « Appartenance » ne se traduit pas par « appurtenance » (terme juridique rare). « To belong » se construit avec « to » ou un lieu : « they feel they belong here ».

def: The feeling of loyalty and willingness to cooperate that holds the members of a team together.

formal.ex: The move to hybrid working has put [[team cohesion]] under strain.

everyday.ex: There's a great [[team spirit]] in the Lyon office.

informal.ex: It took a few months, but the new team has really started [[to gel]].

note_fr: « Cohesion » existe mais « team spirit » est bien plus courant à l'oral. « To gel » (prendre, se souder) se dit d'une équipe qui commence à bien fonctionner ensemble.

def: To increase the commitment, energy and involvement that employees bring to their work.

formal.ex: The plan sets out six measures [[to strengthen employee engagement]] next year.

everyday.ex: Free breakfasts won't [[boost engagement]] if the real problem is workload.

note_fr: En anglais RH, « engagement » = implication dans le travail, pas « promesse » ni « embauche ». « Engagement levels » (niveaux d'engagement) est la collocation standard dans les rapports.

def: No longer interested in or committed to one's work, and doing only what is strictly necessary.

formal.ex: A significant minority of respondents appear [[disengaged]] from their work.

everyday.ex: He's been [[demotivated]] ever since the reorganisation.
everyday.ex_us: He's been [[unmotivated]] ever since the reorganization.

informal.ex: You can tell when someone has [[checked out]] - they do the minimum and leave on the dot.

note_fr: « Démotivé » : « demotivated » (UK) ou « unmotivated » (US). « Checked out » (familier) décrit quelqu'un encore présent physiquement mais plus mentalement. À ne pas confondre avec « to check out » d'un hôtel.

fr: en faire plus que demandé, se surpasser
def: To make more effort than is expected or required of you.

formal.ex: The award recognises colleagues who have [[made an exceptional contribution]] this year.
formal.ex_us: The award recognizes colleagues who have [[made an exceptional contribution]] this year.

everyday.ex: She always [[goes the extra mile]] for new joiners.

informal.ex: The IT team [[bent over backwards]] to get everyone set up before the move.

collocations: to be willing to go the extra mile
to put in the extra effort
note_fr: Expression très courante dans les messages de remerciement. Variante américaine fréquente : « to go above and beyond ». Ne pas confondre avec « to go too far » (aller trop loin).

fr: sens au travail, travail porteur de sens
def: Work that people feel is worthwhile and that gives them a sense of purpose.

formal.ex: Younger employees increasingly expect [[meaningful work]] as well as fair pay.

everyday.ex: People here have a real [[sense of purpose]] - they know why their job matters.

informal.ex: Our care staff want to feel they [[make a difference]], not just fill in forms.

collocations: to find meaning in one's work
note_fr: « Le sens au travail » ne se dit pas « the sense of work ». Dites « meaningful work » ou « a sense of purpose ». « Sense » seul = sensation ou bon sens.

fr: avoir son mot à dire, avoir voix au chapitre
def: To have the right or the opportunity to influence a decision.

formal.ex: Employees should [[be involved in decision-making]] on matters that affect their daily work.

everyday.ex: If people [[have a say]] in how the office is laid out, they're far more likely to use it.

note_fr: « Say » est ici un nom. Comparez « to have one's say » (donner son avis) et « to have a say in something » (avoir voix au chapitre, peser sur la décision).

def: The ways in which employees express their views and influence decisions, whether directly or through representatives.

formal.ex: We have strengthened the channels through which [[employee voice]] reaches the executive committee.

everyday.ex: Frontline staff have very few ways [[to make themselves heard]].

note_fr: « Employee voice » désigne l'ensemble des moyens par lesquels les salariés s'expriment (enquêtes, représentants, réunions). À distinguer du droit d'expression directe et collective, notion légale française.

fr: droit d'expression directe et collective des salariés

term.uk: right of direct and collective expression
term.us: right of direct and collective expression

def: A French statutory right allowing employees to express their views directly and as a group, rather than through representatives, on the content, conditions and organisation of their work.

formal.uk: right of direct and collective expression
formal.us: right of direct and collective expression
formal.ex: Arrangements for exercising the [[right of direct and collective expression]] are set out in Appendix 2.

everyday.uk: space to talk about the work
everyday.us: space to talk about the work
everyday.ex: We've set up monthly sessions to give teams [[space to talk about the work]] itself.

collocations: to exercise the right of expression
note_fr: Notion propre au droit français, distincte de la liberté d'expression (« freedom of expression ») et de la représentation du personnel. Expliquez-la plutôt que de la traduire mot à mot.

explain.written: French law gives employees a right to express their views directly and collectively on the content, conditions and organisation of their work, without going through their representatives.
explain.spoken: In France, employees have a legal right to get together and say how their work could be organised better - directly, not through the unions.

def: A regular survey that measures how employees feel about their work, their managers and the organisation.

formal.ex: The annual [[employee opinion survey]] will run from 2 to 20 March.
formal.ex_us: The annual [[employee opinion survey]] will run from March 2 to 20.

everyday.ex: Have you filled in the [[staff survey]] yet?
everyday.ex_us: Have you filled out the [[employee survey]] yet?

collocations: to take part in the survey
note_fr: Faux ami : « social barometer » n'est pas compris. « Social » en anglais renvoie à la vie en société ou aux loisirs, pas aux relations de travail. Notez aussi « to fill in » (UK) / « to fill out » (US) un questionnaire.

def: The percentage of people invited to take part in a survey who actually complete it.

formal.ex: The [[response rate]] rose to 78%, the highest since the survey was introduced.

everyday.ex: We need to push the [[participation rate]] up in the warehouses.

note_fr: « Taux de participation » à une enquête = « response rate ». « Turnout » est réservé aux élections. Ne confondez pas avec « turnover » (rotation du personnel).

def: The answers that survey respondents write in their own words, as opposed to the scores they give.

formal.ex: Over 1,200 [[open-ended responses]] were analysed by theme.
formal.ex_us: Over 1,200 [[open-ended responses]] were analyzed by theme.

everyday.ex: The scores look fine, but the [[free-text comments]] tell a different story.

note_fr: Faux ami : « verbatims » (nom pluriel) n'existe pas en anglais. « Verbatim » est un adjectif ou un adverbe (« verbatim quotes », « to quote verbatim »). Dites « comments » ou « free-text responses ».

def: The factors that have the strongest influence on how engaged employees are, such as career prospects, recognition or trust in management.

formal.ex: Career development emerged as the strongest of the [[drivers of engagement]] identified.

everyday.ex: Pay isn't one of our top [[engagement drivers]], surprisingly.

note_fr: « Levier » se traduit rarement par « lever » dans ce contexte : on parle de « drivers ». « To drive » = faire progresser, pas seulement conduire.

def: The minimum number of respondents a group must have before its survey results are reported, so that no individual can be identified.

formal.ex: No results are reported for teams below the [[anonymity threshold]] of five respondents.

everyday.ex: His team's too small - it's below the [[minimum group size]], so he won't get a report.

note_fr: Garantie essentielle pour la confiance des répondants. « Anonymous » (anonyme) ≠ « confidential » (identifiable par le prestataire mais jamais communiqué) : ne promettez pas l'un pour l'autre.

fr: eNPS (propension des salariés à recommander l'entreprise)
def: An indicator based on how likely employees say they are to recommend the organisation as a place to work.

formal.ex: Our [[employee net promoter score]] stands at +12, against +4 last year.

everyday.ex: What's our [[eNPS]] looking like this quarter?

note_fr: Indicateur fondé sur une seule question (« Recommanderiez-vous l'entreprise comme employeur ? »). Se prononce lettre par lettre : /ˌiː en piː ˈes/. Le score peut être négatif.

def: A document listing the steps to be taken, by whom and by when, to achieve a goal or respond to a problem.

formal.ex: Each department will draw up an [[action plan]] by the end of June.

everyday.ex: Let's agree on three [[next steps]] before we leave the room.

collocations: to draw up an action plan
note_fr: « Plan d'actions » au pluriel en français, mais « action plan » au singulier en anglais (le premier nom est invariable). Le responsable d'une action = « action owner ».

fr: « vous avez dit, nous avons fait » (restitution des suites données)
def: A way of reporting back to employees that links what they said in a survey or consultation to the changes made in response.

formal.uk: to report back on the actions taken
formal.us: to report back on the actions taken
formal.ex: Management will [[report back on the actions taken]] within six months of the survey.

everyday.ex: We're putting a [[you said, we did]] poster up in every canteen.
everyday.ex_us: We're putting a [[you said, we did]] poster up in every break room.

informal.ex: If we don't [[close the loop]], nobody will bother filling it in next year.

note_fr: Format très répandu au Royaume-Uni pour montrer les suites d'une enquête. « To close the loop » = boucler la boucle, faire un retour à ceux qui ont donné leur avis. « Restituer » ne se traduit pas par « to restitute » (rendre un bien).

def: A system or practice in which colleagues, not only managers, publicly thank and acknowledge each other's work.

formal.ex: The new platform enables [[peer-to-peer recognition]] across all our sites.

everyday.ex: Anyone can [[thank a colleague publicly]] on the platform.

informal.ex: Big [[shout-out]] to the payroll team for getting everyone paid on time.

note_fr: « Shout-out » (remerciement public) est très courant à l'oral et sur les messageries internes, surtout aux États-Unis ; à éviter dans un écrit formel.

def: A gift or distinction given to an employee to mark a significant number of years with the organisation.

formal.ex: Twelve employees will receive a [[long-service award]] at the ceremony.
formal.ex_us: Twelve employees will receive a [[service award]] at the ceremony.

everyday.ex: Happy [[work anniversary]], Priya - ten years already!

note_fr: La médaille d'honneur du travail est une distinction officielle française, sans équivalent public au Royaume-Uni ou aux États-Unis, où les « long-service awards » sont décidés par l'entreprise. Expliquez-la si vous en parlez.

def: The way an organisation shares information with its employees and enables them to share information with each other.

formal.ex: Responsibility for [[internal communication]] lies with the Communications Director.

everyday.ex: Can you run the draft past [[internal comms]] before it goes out?

note_fr: « Communication » est indénombrable dans ce sens. « Comms » est l'abréviation courante (UK et US) pour le service comme pour l'activité. « To run something past someone » = soumettre pour avis.

def: An email sent to every employee in the organisation at once.

formal.ex: A [[message to all staff]] will be sent by the Chief Executive at 9 a.m.
formal.ex_us: A [[message to all employees]] will be sent by the CEO at 9 a.m.

everyday.ex: Did you see the [[all-staff email]] about the new canteen?
everyday.ex_us: Did you see the [[company-wide email]] about the new cafeteria?

note_fr: « Collaborateurs » ne se traduit pas par « collaborators », qui évoque la complicité (voire la collaboration avec l'ennemi) : dites « staff », « employees » ou « colleagues ».

def: A regular publication, usually digital, that keeps employees up to date with news from the organisation.

formal.ex: The [[staff newsletter]] is published on the first Monday of each month.
formal.ex_us: The [[employee newsletter]] is published on the first Monday of each month.

everyday.ex: Could we get a piece in the [[newsletter]] about the volunteering day?

collocations: to write a piece for the newsletter
note_fr: Un article de newsletter = « a piece », « a feature » ou « an item ». Le journal interne imprimé : « in-house magazine ». Prononciation US : /ˈnuːz-/, UK : /ˈnjuːz-/.

def: A board on a wall where official notices and information for staff are displayed.

formal.ex: The agreement will be displayed on the staff [[noticeboard]] at each site.
formal.ex_us: The agreement will be displayed on the staff [[bulletin board]] at each site.

everyday.ex: Can you [[put up a notice]] in the warehouse about the blood drive?
everyday.ex_us: Can you [[post a notice]] in the warehouse about the blood drive?

note_fr: UK « noticeboard », US « bulletin board ». Afficher = « to put up » (UK) ou « to post » (US). Pour les salariés sans adresse e-mail (atelier, entrepôt), l'affichage reste un canal essentiel.

def: A private website, accessible only to employees, where an organisation shares documents, news and tools.

formal.ex: The full policy is available on the [[intranet]].

everyday.ex: We'll [[put the slides up]] on the intranet after the meeting.
everyday.ex_us: We'll [[post the slides]] on the intranet after the meeting.

collocations: to find something on the intranet
note_fr: Préposition : « on the intranet » (pas « in »). Accent tonique sur la première syllabe : /ˈɪn-/.

fr: donner la parole à la salle
def: To invite the audience at a meeting or presentation to ask questions or make comments.

formal.uk: to open the floor to questions
formal.us: to open the floor to questions
formal.ex: I will now [[open the floor to questions]].

everyday.ex: I'll talk for ten minutes and then [[take questions]].

informal.ex: Right, let's [[throw it open]] - who wants to go first?

collocations: to hand over to the audience
note_fr: « The floor » = l'assistance, la salle. « Questions from the floor » = questions du public. « To have the floor » = avoir la parole.

def: Part of a meeting or event in which the audience asks questions and the speakers answer them.

formal.ex: The presentation will be followed by a [[question-and-answer session]].

everyday.ex: We'll keep twenty minutes at the end for [[Q&A]].

informal.ex: The CEO's doing an [[ask-me-anything session]] on Thursday.

note_fr: Prononcez « Q and A » /ˌkjuː ən ˈeɪ/. « Ask me anything » vient des forums en ligne : format informel où le dirigeant accepte toutes les questions.

def: A short meeting in which a manager passes on information to the team and answers questions.

formal.ex: Managers will hold a [[team briefing]] within 24 hours of the announcement.

everyday.ex: Let's have a [[quick catch-up]] at nine to go through it.
everyday.ex_us: Let's have a [[huddle]] at nine to go through it.

note_fr: « Briefing » = réunion d'information (ou note d'information), alors que « brief » = cahier des charges, consignes. « Huddle » (US) = point rapide, souvent debout.

def: A set of materials, such as key messages, a script, slides and FAQs, given to managers so that they can pass on a message to their teams consistently.

formal.ex: A [[manager briefing pack]] will be sent to all people managers on Monday.
formal.ex_us: A [[manager communication toolkit]] will be sent to all people managers on Monday.

everyday.ex: Everything you need is in the [[toolkit]] - slides, FAQs and a short script.

collocations: to send out a briefing pack
note_fr: « Kit » s'emploie (« comms kit »), mais « briefing pack » (UK) et « toolkit » (US) sont plus naturels. Un kit managérial contient en général des « talking points », une FAQ et un calendrier.

def: To give employees regular updates so that they know what is happening.

formal.ex: We undertake [[to keep employees informed]] at each stage of the project.

everyday.ex: I'll [[keep you posted]] as soon as I hear anything.

informal.uk: to keep someone in the loop
informal.us: to keep someone in the loop
informal.ex: Just [[keep me in the loop]], will you?

collocations: to keep people up to date
note_fr: « Informer » se dit « to inform » à l'écrit, mais à l'oral « to let someone know » ou « to keep someone posted » sont bien plus naturels. « To inform » ne s'emploie pas sans complément de personne.

def: To tell someone about something important and usually unpleasant.

formal.ex: It is with regret that we must [[inform staff of]] the closure of the Nantes branch.

everyday.ex: Who's going to [[break the news]] to the team?

informal.ex: He [[dropped a bombshell]] right at the end of the meeting.

note_fr: « To break the news » s'emploie presque toujours pour une mauvaise nouvelle. « News » est indénombrable et singulier : « the news is bad ». « Annonce » ≠ « advertisement » (publicité).

def: To communicate an idea successfully so that people understand it.

formal.ex: The letter must [[convey the message]] clearly and without ambiguity.

everyday.ex: Short videos [[get the message across]] better than long emails.

informal.ex: The town hall didn't really [[land the message]].

note_fr: « To get across » = faire comprendre. « To land » (jargon d'entreprise) = que le message soit bien reçu. « Passer un message » ≠ « to pass on a message » (transmettre le message de quelqu'un).

def: To be honest and open about something from the start, rather than hiding it.

formal.ex: We intend [[to be transparent about]] the reasons for this decision.

everyday.ex: It's better [[to be upfront about]] what we don't know yet.

informal.uk: to tell it like it is
informal.us: to tell it like it is
informal.ex: People respect her because she [[tells it like it is]].

collocations: to be honest about the uncertainty
note_fr: « Upfront » = franc, direct (et aussi « payé d'avance » dans « upfront payment »). « Transparent » existe mais est surexploité dans les communications d'entreprise.

def: To deal with the worries that people have expressed, by giving information or taking action.

formal.ex: This FAQ seeks [[to address the concerns]] raised by employees at the meeting.

everyday.uk: to put people's minds at rest
everyday.us: to put people's minds at rest
everyday.ex: A clear timetable would [[put people's minds at rest]].

note_fr: « To address » = traiter, répondre à (pas « adresser »). « Concerns » = inquiétudes. « To allay fears » (apaiser les craintes) est plus soutenu.

def: To make sure that people do not expect more than can realistically be delivered.

formal.ex: It will be important [[to manage expectations]] regarding the pace of change.

everyday.ex: Let's be careful [[not to overpromise]] - we can't fix everything this year.

informal.ex: The rule is simple: [[under-promise and over-deliver]].

note_fr: « Expectations » = attentes (faux ami partiel avec « expectative »). « To set expectations » = fixer le cadre ; « to manage expectations » = éviter les déceptions.

def: Communication designed to explain a change to employees, help them understand its reasons and support them through it.

formal.ex: A dedicated [[change communication]] plan will accompany the roll-out.

everyday.ex: People cope better with change when we [[explain the why]], not just the what.

note_fr: « Accompagner le changement » : dites « to support people through change » plutôt que « to accompany the change » (calque). « Rationale » (/ˌræʃəˈnɑːl/) = justification.

def: Employees chosen or volunteering to promote a change within their teams, relay information and collect feedback.

formal.ex: A [[change network]] of forty volunteers will relay information in each department.

everyday.ex: We've recruited [[change champions]] on every site to answer questions.

collocations: to set up a network of champions
note_fr: « Ambassadors » se dit aussi, mais « champions » est très courant en entreprise. « To champion something » = défendre, porter un projet.

def: A small group of senior people who take charge of decisions and communication when a serious incident occurs.

formal.ex: The [[crisis management team]] met at 7 a.m. to agree the initial response.
formal.ex_us: The [[crisis management team]] met at 7 a.m. to agree on the initial response.

everyday.ex: The [[crisis team]] is meeting again at two.

note_fr: « Cellule de crise » ne se dit pas « crisis cell » (peu compris). Préférez « crisis team » ou « crisis management team ». Notez « to agree something » (UK) / « to agree on something » (US).

def: The way an organisation communicates with employees and other audiences during a serious, unexpected event.

formal.ex: Our [[crisis communication]] protocol sets out who speaks, to whom and when.

everyday.ex: Our priority is [[to get the facts out]] before the rumours take over.
everyday.ex_us: Our priority is [[to get the facts out]] before the rumors take over.

note_fr: En crise, les salariés doivent être informés avant ou en même temps que l'extérieur : ils sont les premiers relais, et les premiers lecteurs des réseaux sociaux. « Media enquiries » (UK) / « media inquiries » (US).

def: A short statement issued quickly after an incident, before all the facts are known, to acknowledge the situation and say that action is being taken.

formal.ex: A [[holding statement]] was issued to staff within the hour.

everyday.ex: Send managers a [[holding line]] for now; we'll update them at four.

note_fr: Structure type : on reconnaît la situation, on montre qu'on agit, on annonce quand viendra la prochaine information. Ne spéculez jamais sur les causes dans un « holding statement ».

term.uk: to get ahead of the story
term.us: to get ahead of the story

def: To communicate about a situation before others do, so that you control how it is first presented.

formal.ex: We recommend [[communicating proactively]] before the information reaches the press.

everyday.uk: to get ahead of the story
everyday.us: to get ahead of the story
everyday.ex: If we don't [[get ahead of the story]], staff will read about it on social media first.

informal.uk: to get out in front of it
informal.us: to get out in front of it
informal.ex: We need [[to get out in front of this]] today.

note_fr: Dans un contexte français, prendre les devants ne doit jamais conduire à informer les salariés avant les représentants du personnel lorsque ceux-ci doivent l'être en premier.

def: To keep to the agreed key points when speaking, without improvising or speculating.

formal.uk: to adhere to the agreed messages
formal.us: to adhere to the agreed messages
formal.ex: Managers are asked [[to adhere to the agreed messages]] and not to speculate.

everyday.ex: Whatever they ask, [[stay on message]] and don't guess.

informal.ex: If you're unsure, just [[stick to the script]].

collocations: to keep to the agreed lines
note_fr: « On message » = conforme à la ligne convenue ; « off message » = hors ligne. Pour briefer les managers sans les infantiliser, expliquez aussi le pourquoi des messages.

fr: séquencement de l'annonce (représentants du personnel avant salariés)
def: The order in which different groups, such as employee representatives, managers, staff and the outside world, are told about a decision or project.

formal.ex: The [[sequencing of announcements]] must ensure that the works council is informed before employees.

everyday.ex: Before we write a word, we need to agree [[who hears what first]].

informal.ex: Please keep this [[under wraps]] until Thursday.

note_fr: En France, présenter aux salariés comme définitive une décision sur laquelle le CSE doit être informé ou consulté peut constituer un délit d'entrave. D'où l'ordre habituel : CSE, managers, salariés, puis extérieur.

def: To answer questions, often difficult or unexpected ones, from an audience.

formal.ex: The HR Director will [[respond to questions]] from employees at the end of the session.

everyday.ex: She [[fielded questions]] for forty minutes without notes.

collocations: to field questions from the floor
note_fr: « To field » vient du cricket et du base-ball : rattraper la balle. Le verbe suggère qu'on répond avec aisance à des questions imprévues.

def: A question that is difficult to answer, especially in public, because it is sensitive or unexpected.

formal.ex: Speakers should prepare for [[challenging questions]] on job security.

everyday.ex: Expect a [[tricky question]] about the bonus.

informal.ex: Someone's bound to throw you a [[curveball]] about the car park.
informal.ex_us: Someone's bound to throw you a [[curveball]] about the parking lot.

note_fr: « Curveball » vient du base-ball (balle à effet) : « to throw someone a curveball » = déstabiliser. « Question piège » ne se dit pas « trap question ». « A loaded question » = une question orientée.

def: Showing a lack of awareness of how people feel, especially in a public message.

formal.ex: Announcing record bonuses during a pay freeze was widely perceived as [[insensitive]].

everyday.ex: Sending that video the day after the redundancies was completely [[tone-deaf]].
everyday.ex_us: Sending that video the day after the layoffs was completely [[tone-deaf]].

informal.ex: The CEO's email really [[missed the mark]].

note_fr: Au sens propre : qui chante faux. Au figuré : qui ne perçoit pas l'état d'esprit de son public. Critique fréquente des communications de direction en période difficile.

def: To present bad news in a way that makes it seem less unpleasant than it really is.

formal.ex: The message should neither dramatise nor [[minimise]] the situation.
formal.ex_us: The message should neither dramatize nor [[minimize]] the situation.

everyday.ex: Don't [[sugar-coat]] it - people can tell.

informal.ex: Staff will see straight through any attempt [[to spin]] the figures.

collocations: to put a positive spin on
note_fr: « Spin » = présentation orientée (vocabulaire politique). Les salariés détectent vite l'enrobage : en communication interne, la franchise paie davantage.

term.uk: to address the elephant in the room
term.us: to address the elephant in the room

ipa.uk: /tə əˌdres ði ˌelɪfənt ɪn ðə ˈruːm/
ipa.us: /tə əˌdres ði ˌeləfənt ɪn ðə ˈruːm/

def: To talk openly about an obvious problem that everyone is aware of but nobody wants to mention.

formal.ex: The Chief Executive chose [[to address the issue directly]] in her opening remarks.

everyday.uk: to address the elephant in the room
everyday.us: to address the elephant in the room
everyday.ex: Let me [[address the elephant in the room]]: yes, the Lyon site is part of the review.

note_fr: Nommer d'emblée le sujet que tout le monde attend, en début de réunion plénière, désamorce souvent l'hostilité. « Head-on » = de front.

fr: présence (visibilité) de la direction sur le terrain
def: The practice of senior leaders being present, accessible and seen by employees, especially during difficult periods.

formal.ex: Employees have asked for more [[visible leadership]] during the transition.

everyday.ex: He tries [[to walk the floor]] every Friday morning.

note_fr: « To walk the floor » (aller sur le terrain, dans les ateliers ou les plateaux). Dans les enquêtes, le manque de visibilité de la direction est un irritant classique.

fr: réunion avec le N+2 (sans le N+1)
def: A meeting between a senior manager and employees who report to one of that manager's direct reports.

formal.ex: Directors will hold quarterly [[skip-level meetings]] with team members.

everyday.ex: I've got a [[skip-level]] with the VP on Tuesday.

note_fr: Pratique d'origine américaine. « N+1 / N+2 » ne s'emploient pas en anglais : dites « my manager », « my manager's manager » ou « my boss's boss ».

fr: règles de bonne conduite en réunion hybride
def: Simple shared rules that make meetings fair and effective when some participants are in the room and others are remote.

formal.ex: The guide sets out simple rules of [[hybrid meeting etiquette]].

everyday.ex: We've agreed it's [[cameras on]] for team meetings.

collocations: to give remote participants a voice
note_fr: « Etiquette » s'écrit sans accent. « Remote-first » : tout le monde se connecte depuis son poste, même au bureau, pour éviter que les participants à distance soient relégués.

def: Regular shared moments, such as a weekly meeting or a monthly lunch, that help a team stay connected.

formal.ex: Managers are encouraged to establish regular [[team rituals]], such as a weekly check-in.

everyday.ex: Our Monday [[weekly catch-up]] is the only time we're all together.

note_fr: « Rituals » est compris, mais « routines » ou « traditions » sonnent souvent plus naturel. Un point régulier = « a check-in » ou « a catch-up ».

def: A day or more spent away from the usual workplace, for a team to reflect, plan and build relationships.

formal.ex: The [[team away day]] will be held at a venue near Reims.
formal.ex_us: The [[team offsite]] will be held at a venue near Reims.

everyday.ex: We're planning an [[away day]] in June.
everyday.ex_us: We're planning an [[offsite]] in June.

note_fr: « Séminaire » ≠ « seminar » (cours, conférence). Au Royaume-Uni : « away day » ; aux États-Unis : « offsite », ou « retreat » pour plusieurs jours.

fr: échanges informels (à la machine à café)
def: The casual conversations colleagues have when they bump into each other at work, which help information and relationships to flow.

formal.ex: Remote work reduces the [[informal interactions]] through which knowledge is shared.

everyday.ex: New joiners miss out on the [[watercooler conversations]].

informal.uk: a chat by the coffee machine
informal.us: a chat by the coffee machine
informal.ex: Half our decisions used to get made over [[a chat by the coffee machine]].

note_fr: Image américaine de la fontaine à eau, équivalent de notre machine à café. C'est l'argument classique des défenseurs du retour au bureau ; « to bump into » = croiser par hasard.

fr: flex office (bureaux partagés sans poste attribué)
def: A way of organising an office in which employees do not have their own desk but use whichever one is available.

formal.ex: The new premises will operate on a [[desk-sharing]] basis, with seven desks for every ten employees.

everyday.ex: Nobody likes [[hot-desking]] when it means hunting for a seat at nine.

note_fr: « Flex office » est un anglicisme français peu employé en anglais. Dites « hot-desking » ou « desk sharing » ; aux États-Unis, « hoteling » désigne la réservation de postes.

def: A large office space without walls or private offices, shared by many employees.

formal.ex: Most teams work in an [[open-plan office]] on the third floor.
formal.ex_us: Most teams work in an [[open office]] on the third floor.

everyday.ex: The noise in the [[open-plan]] is getting to people.
everyday.ex_us: The noise in the [[open office]] is getting to people.

note_fr: Faux ami : « open space » désigne en anglais un espace vert ou un terrain non bâti. Pour le bureau, dites « open-plan office » (UK) ou « open office » (US).

def: A service at work that handles everyday errands for employees, such as dry cleaning, parcels or shoe repairs.

formal.ex: Employees have access to a [[workplace concierge service]] for dry cleaning, parcels and shoe repairs.

everyday.ex: You can leave your shoes with the [[concierge]] - they'll be ready by Thursday.

note_fr: Faux ami : en anglais, « concierge » évoque l'accueil d'un grand hôtel, pas un gardien d'immeuble (« caretaker » UK, « superintendent » US). « Conciergerie » n'existe pas en anglais.

fr: joindre le geste à la parole
def: To act in a way that is consistent with what you say or promise.

formal.ex: Management will be judged on its ability [[to match words with action]].

everyday.ex: We talk a lot about wellbeing, but are we [[walking the talk]]?

informal.uk: to put one's money where one's mouth is
informal.us: to put one's money where one's mouth is
informal.ex: If they care about wellbeing, they should [[put their money where their mouth is]].

note_fr: « To practise what you preach » (UK) / « practice » (US) a le même sens. « Put your money where your mouth is » = mettre les moyens financiers derrière ses promesses.

def: A set of activities and services offered by an employer to support employees' physical, mental and financial health.

formal.ex: The [[wellbeing programme]] includes workshops, sports activities and a confidential helpline.
formal.ex_us: The [[wellness program]] includes workshops, sports activities and a confidential support line.

everyday.ex: Fruit bowls are nice, but [[wellbeing initiatives]] won't fix a workload problem.
everyday.ex_us: Fruit bowls are nice, but [[wellness initiatives]] won't fix a workload problem.

note_fr: UK « wellbeing programme », US « wellness program » (souvent lié à l'assurance santé). « Take-up » (UK) / « utilization » (US) = taux d'utilisation. Les salariés jugent ces programmes à l'aune de leur charge de travail réelle.

def: A free telephone service through which employees can speak in confidence to a trained counsellor or adviser.

formal.ex: A free, [[confidential helpline]] is available 24 hours a day, seven days a week.
formal.ex_us: A free, [[confidential support line]] is available 24 hours a day, seven days a week.

everyday.ex: The main thing is that people know there's [[someone to talk to]].

note_fr: Ne confondez pas avec le dispositif d'alerte (« reporting hotline »), qui sert à signaler des manquements. La ligne d'écoute fait souvent partie d'un programme d'aide aux salariés (EAP). « Counsellor » (UK) / « counselor » (US).

def: An employee trained to recognise signs of mental distress in colleagues, offer initial support and direct them to professional help.

formal.ex: Forty [[mental health first aiders]] have been trained across the network.

everyday.ex: If you're struggling, have a word with your local [[wellbeing champion]].
everyday.ex_us: If you're struggling, talk to your local [[well-being champion]].

collocations: to train as a mental health first aider
note_fr: Le secouriste en santé mentale écoute et oriente ; il ne pose pas de diagnostic et ne remplace ni le médecin du travail ni la prévention des risques psychosociaux.

def: To direct someone to the service or person that can help them.

formal.ex: Managers are not counsellors; their role is [[to signpost employees to]] appropriate support.
formal.ex_us: Managers are not counselors; their role is [[to refer employees to]] appropriate support.

everyday.uk: to point someone in the right direction
everyday.us: to point someone in the right direction
everyday.ex: If you don't know the answer, just [[point them in the right direction]].

note_fr: « To signpost » est très britannique ; aux États-Unis on dit plutôt « to refer » ou « to direct someone to ». Rappel utile pour les managers : orienter, ce n'est pas jouer les thérapeutes.

fr: mesures en faveur de la parentalité
def: Workplace measures that help employees combine work with bringing up children, such as flexible hours, childcare support or coaching for new parents.

formal.ex: The Group has strengthened its [[family-friendly policies]], including support for adoptive parents.

everyday.ex: We're losing good people because there's so little [[support for working parents]].

note_fr: « Parentalité » ne se traduit pas par « parentality » (inexistant) : dites « parenthood » ou « being a working parent ». Les règles de congés relèvent d'un autre thème ; ici, il s'agit d'accompagnement.

def: A childcare facility provided or reserved by an employer for the young children of its staff.

formal.ex: The company reserves [[workplace nursery places]] for employees' children.
formal.ex_us: The company offers [[employer-sponsored child care]] for employees' children.

everyday.ex: She only came back full-time because she got a [[nursery place]].
everyday.ex_us: She only came back full-time because she got a [[daycare spot]].

collocations: to reserve places in a nursery
note_fr: En anglais britannique, « crèche » désigne surtout la crèche de Noël ! Dites « nursery » (UK) ou « daycare » / « child care » (US).

def: An employee who, alongside their job, looks after a family member or friend who is ill, disabled or elderly.

formal.ex: The guide explains the support available to any [[employee with caring responsibilities]].
formal.ex_us: The guide explains the support available to any [[employee with caregiving responsibilities]].

everyday.ex: We had no idea how many [[working carers]] we had until we asked.
everyday.ex_us: We had no idea how many [[working caregivers]] we had until we asked.

note_fr: « Aidant » = « carer » (UK) ou « caregiver » (US). Ne confondez pas avec « care worker » (aide-soignant, auxiliaire de vie), qui est un métier.

def: The extent to which employees feel secure and in control of their money, now and in the future.

formal.ex: Our [[financial wellbeing]] programme offers free, confidential guidance on budgeting and debt.
formal.ex_us: Our [[financial well-being]] program offers free, confidential guidance on budgeting and debt.

everyday.ex: [[Money worries]] are now the main source of stress mentioned in the survey.

informal.ex: A lot of younger staff are [[strapped for cash]] by the end of the month.

note_fr: UK « wellbeing » (souvent en un mot), US « well-being ». « Financial education » = éducation financière ; « debt advice » = conseil en cas d'endettement.

def: To have just enough money to pay for the things you need.

formal.uk: to meet one's essential living costs
formal.us: to meet one's essential living costs
formal.ex: Some employees report difficulty [[meeting their essential living costs]].

everyday.ex: With rents going up, some of our warehouse staff are struggling [[to make ends meet]].

informal.uk: to live from payday to payday
informal.ex: Plenty of people [[live from payday to payday]].
informal.ex_us: Plenty of people [[live paycheck to paycheck]].

collocations: to struggle to make ends meet
note_fr: Même image qu'en français, avec un verbe différent : « make », pas « join ». « Cost of living » = coût de la vie ; « cost-of-living crisis » est une expression très britannique.

def: A sum of money that each employee can spend on approved activities such as sport, relaxation or learning.

formal.ex: Each employee receives an annual [[wellbeing allowance]] of 300 euros for sport or relaxation.
formal.ex_us: Each employee gets a [[lifestyle spending account]] worth 300 euros a year for sport or relaxation.

everyday.ex: I spent my [[wellbeing pot]] on a yoga course.
everyday.ex_us: I used my [[LSA]] on a yoga class.

note_fr: En France, avant de lancer ce type d'avantage, vérifiez son traitement social (cotisations) et son articulation avec les activités sociales et culturelles gérées par le CSE.

def: A company's commitment to managing the social and environmental effects of its activities and to acting responsibly towards its employees and society.

formal.ex: The Board reviews the Group's [[corporate social responsibility]] strategy every year.

everyday.ex: She's moved from HR into the [[CSR]] team.

note_fr: Dans CSR, « social » renvoie à la société au sens large. Les grandes entreprises parlent de plus en plus de « sustainability » ou d'« ESG ». Sigle prononcé /ˌsiː es ˈɑː/ (UK), /ˌsiː es ˈɑːr/ (US).

def: Acting in a way that meets present needs without harming people, the environment or the ability of future generations to meet their own needs.

formal.ex: [[Sustainability]] is now a standing item on the executive committee agenda.

everyday.ex: Staff are keen on [[going green]], but they want to see real changes, not posters.

note_fr: « Développement durable » se dit « sustainable development » pour les politiques publiques, mais en entreprise on dit « sustainability ». Faux ami : « durable » en anglais = robuste, résistant.

def: Environmental, social and governance factors, used by investors and others to assess a company's sustainability and conduct.

formal.ex: Investors increasingly assess companies on [[environmental, social and governance]] criteria.

everyday.ex: Our [[ESG]] rating came up at the investor meeting.

note_fr: Le « S » d'ESG couvre les salariés (santé-sécurité, formation, égalité, dialogue social) mais aussi les clients et les communautés. C'est souvent la RH qui fournit ces données.

def: The part of a sustainability strategy or report that deals with people: employees, workers in the supply chain, communities and customers.

formal.ex: Under the [[social pillar]], the Group reports on headcount, training, health and safety and diversity.

everyday.ex: HR owns most of [[the S in ESG]].

note_fr: « Pillar » est l'usage établi. « Volet social » peut aussi se rendre par « the social dimension » ou, à l'oral, « the people side ».

def: The publication by a company of information on its environmental, social and governance performance and impacts.

formal.ex: [[Sustainability reporting]] requirements now extend to detailed information on the company's own workforce.

everyday.ex: Who's pulling together the HR figures for the [[non-financial reporting]]?

note_fr: « Extra-financier » se traduit par « non-financial » (terme ancien) ou « sustainability » (terme actuel). « Disclosure » = information publiée, pas « divulgation » au sens négatif.

fr: CSRD (directive européenne sur le reporting de durabilité)
def: An EU directive requiring certain companies to publish standardised information on sustainability matters, including their own workforce.

formal.ex: The Group falls within the scope of the [[Corporate Sustainability Reporting Directive]].

everyday.ex: Is the [[CSRD]] going to apply to us, or are we below the thresholds?

collocations: to fall within the scope of
note_fr: Texte européen : le Royaume-Uni et les États-Unis ont leurs propres régimes. Son champ d'application et son calendrier ont été modifiés depuis son adoption : vérifiez toujours les règles en vigueur avant d'affirmer qu'elle s'applique.

def: The principle that a sustainability topic must be reported if it has a significant impact on people or the environment, or a significant financial effect on the company, or both.

formal.ex: The [[double materiality assessment]] identified working conditions as a material topic.

everyday.ex: In plain terms, [[double materiality]] means looking at how we affect people and how issues affect us.

note_fr: « Material » = significatif, important (faux ami partiel avec « matériel »). Notion clé du reporting européen de durabilité.

fr: effectifs propres (personnel de l'entreprise, au sens du reporting)
def: In sustainability reporting, the people who work for the company itself, as opposed to workers employed elsewhere in its value chain.

formal.ex: Disclosures on the company's [[own workforce]] cover working conditions, equal treatment and other work-related rights.

everyday.ex: Before we talk about suppliers, let's look at [[our own people]].

note_fr: Dans le reporting européen, « own workforce » (salariés et certains non-salariés travaillant pour l'entreprise) se distingue de « workers in the value chain » (travailleurs des fournisseurs, sous-traitants, etc.).

def: A French legal obligation on large companies to identify and prevent serious harm to human rights, health and safety and the environment arising from their activities and those of their subsidiaries, subcontractors and suppliers.

formal.ex: The Group's [[duty of vigilance]] extends to subcontractors and suppliers with which it has an established commercial relationship.

everyday.ex: The board wants a clear answer on [[supply chain responsibility]].

collocations: to comply with the duty of vigilance
note_fr: Loi française de 2017, sans équivalent exact au Royaume-Uni ou aux États-Unis, où l'on parle plutôt de « human rights due diligence ». Une directive européenne sur le devoir de vigilance a depuis été adoptée, avec un calendrier qui a évolué.

explain.written: The French duty of vigilance requires large companies to draw up, publish and implement a plan to identify and prevent serious risks to human rights, health and safety and the environment in their own operations and their supply chains.
explain.spoken: It's a French law that makes big groups responsible for checking that their suppliers and subcontractors don't harm people or the environment - and for publishing a plan to show how.

def: The document that French law requires large companies to publish, setting out how they map, assess and mitigate serious risks to people and the environment.

formal.ex: The [[vigilance plan]] includes a risk map, assessment procedures, mitigation measures and an alert mechanism.

everyday.ex: We're updating the [[risk map]] for our logistics subcontractors.

note_fr: Le plan doit aussi rendre compte de sa mise en œuvre effective. La RH y contribue pour les risques liés aux conditions de travail, chez soi et chez les sous-traitants.

explain.written: A vigilance plan is the document French law requires large companies to publish, setting out how they map, assess and mitigate serious risks to human rights, health and safety and the environment, including at their suppliers.
explain.spoken: It's the plan you have to publish to show how you spot and deal with human rights and environmental risks, including at your suppliers.

def: A statement that certain organisations operating in the UK must publish each year, describing the steps they have taken to prevent slavery and human trafficking in their business and supply chains.

formal.ex: Our UK subsidiary publishes an annual [[modern slavery statement]] on its website.

everyday.ex: Legal want HR's input on the [[slavery statement]] by Friday.

note_fr: Obligation britannique (Modern Slavery Act 2015) pour les organisations dépassant un certain seuil de chiffre d'affaires. Pas d'obligation fédérale générale équivalente aux États-Unis. « Forced labour » (UK) / « forced labor » (US).

def: Making misleading claims about how environmentally or socially responsible an organisation is.

formal.ex: The company must avoid [[misleading environmental claims]] in its reporting.

everyday.ex: If we publish that without data, it'll look like [[greenwashing]].

collocations: to back up claims with data
note_fr: Sur le même modèle : « social washing » ou « purpose-washing » (afficher des engagements sociaux sans les tenir). Les salariés sont souvent les premiers à le dénoncer.

def: An activity done only to comply with a rule or appear to do the right thing, without real effect.

formal.ex: The consultation must not be treated as a mere [[formality]].

everyday.ex: If the action plan is just a [[box-ticking exercise]], people will see through it.
everyday.ex_us: If the action plan is just a [[check-the-box exercise]], people will see through it.

note_fr: UK « to tick a box », US « to check a box ». Dans les deux cas, critique d'une démarche formelle sans effet réel. « To go through the motions » = faire le minimum, sans conviction.

def: A short statement of why a company exists and what it aims to contribute, beyond making a profit.

formal.ex: The shareholders approved the inclusion of a [[statement of purpose]] in the articles of association.
formal.ex_us: The shareholders approved the inclusion of a [[statement of purpose]] in the articles of incorporation.

everyday.ex: Our [[purpose]] has to mean something on the shop floor, not just in the annual report.

note_fr: Depuis la loi PACTE (2019), une société française peut inscrire une « raison d'être » dans ses statuts. En anglais, « raison d'être » s'emploie aussi, mais au sens général de justification d'existence.

def: A French company that has written a purpose and specific social and environmental objectives into its articles, with a body to monitor them.

formal.ex: In 2024 the shareholders voted to become a [[mission-led company]].
formal.ex_us: In 2024 the shareholders voted to become a [[mission-driven company]].

everyday.ex: We like to think of ourselves as a [[purpose-driven business]].

note_fr: Statut juridique français (loi PACTE) proche, sans être identique, de la « public benefit corporation » américaine. La certification « B Corp » est un label privé, pas un statut juridique.

explain.written: A société à mission is a French company that has written its purpose and specific social and environmental objectives into its articles, with a mission committee and independent verification of progress.
explain.spoken: It's a legal status in France: the company commits in its articles to social and environmental goals, and someone independent checks whether it delivers.

def: A working day that an employee spends, with the employer's agreement, helping a charity or community project.

formal.ex: Every employee may take two [[paid volunteering days]] a year.
formal.ex_us: Every employee may take two [[paid volunteer days]] a year.

everyday.ex: Our team spent its [[volunteering day]] renovating a youth centre.
everyday.ex_us: Our team spent its [[volunteer day]] renovating a youth center.

collocations: to sign up for a volunteering day
to volunteer with a local charity
note_fr: « Bénévolat » = « volunteering » ; « bénévole » = « volunteer ». Mais « volontariat » au sens RH (se porter volontaire pour un départ) se dit aussi « volunteer » : précisez le contexte.

def: An arrangement in which employees use their professional skills, during working time, to help a charity or public-interest organisation.

formal.ex: Through [[skills-based volunteering]], employees advise local charities during working hours.
formal.ex_us: Through [[skills-based volunteering]], employees advise local nonprofits during working hours.

everyday.ex: Our finance team does a fair amount of [[pro bono work]] for the food bank.

collocations: to second an employee to a charity
note_fr: En France, le mécénat de compétences (mise à disposition de salariés au profit d'un organisme d'intérêt général) peut ouvrir droit à une réduction d'impôt. Faux ami : « patronage » signifie favoritisme ou clientèle, pas mécénat.

def: The ways in which a company contributes to and builds relationships with the local communities where it operates.

formal.ex: Our [[community engagement]] policy focuses on education and employment in the areas where we operate.

everyday.ex: People want [[to give back]] to the town where we've been based for fifty years.

note_fr: « Ancrage territorial » n'a pas d'équivalent direct ; parlez de « local roots » ou de « community engagement ». « Community » désigne ici la population locale, pas une communauté au sens identitaire.

fr: collecter des fonds pour une association
def: To collect money, for example through a sponsored event, and give it to a charitable organisation.

formal.ex: The event [[raised funds for]] three local charities.
formal.ex_us: The event [[raised funds for]] three local nonprofits.

everyday.ex: The Paris office ran a half-marathon [[to raise money for charity]].

note_fr: Une association (loi de 1901) se dit « charity » (UK) ou « nonprofit » (US) ; « association » évoque plutôt un groupement professionnel. « To raise » = collecter (des fonds).

fr: don sur salaire, arrondi sur salaire
def: A scheme that allows employees to give regularly to charity through deductions from their pay.

formal.ex: Employees can donate through the [[payroll giving scheme]].
formal.ex_us: Employees can donate through the [[workplace giving program]].

everyday.ex: You can [[give through payroll]] - it comes straight out of your pay.

collocations: to sign up to payroll giving
note_fr: En France, l'arrondi sur salaire permet de donner quelques centimes ou euros par mois. Au Royaume-Uni, le « payroll giving » bénéficie d'un régime fiscal propre ; aux États-Unis, on parle de « workplace giving ».

def: To help people know more about a subject and understand why it matters.

formal.ex: The campaign aims [[to raise awareness]] of the support available to working carers.

everyday.ex: We need [[to get the word out]] that the helpline exists.

note_fr: « Sensibiliser à » = « to raise awareness of » ; « to sensitise » ne s'emploie pas dans ce sens. « Awareness week » = semaine de sensibilisation.

def: A voluntary group of employees who share a characteristic or interest, such as parents, women in engineering or LGBT+ staff, and support each other at work.

formal.ex: The women's [[employee network]] now has members in twelve countries.
formal.ex_us: The women's [[employee resource group]] now has members in twelve countries.

everyday.ex: She co-chairs the LGBT+ [[staff network]].
everyday.ex_us: She co-chairs the LGBTQ+ [[ERG]].

note_fr: Aux États-Unis, « ERG » est le terme établi ; au Royaume-Uni, « staff network » ou « employee network ». Ces réseaux naissent de l'initiative des salariés, avec le soutien de la direction.

def: Wording that avoids excluding or stereotyping people, for example by using gender-neutral terms.

formal.ex: The communications guide recommends [[inclusive language]] in all internal materials.

everyday.ex: We've switched to [[gender-neutral wording]] in the intranet templates.

note_fr: « Inclusive language » ne correspond pas à l'« écriture inclusive » française (point médian) : en anglais, il s'agit surtout de formulations neutres (« they », « chair », « staff ») et de termes non stigmatisants.

def: To mark achievements, large or small, so that people feel their work is recognised.

formal.ex: It is important [[to celebrate successes]], however small.

everyday.ex: We [[celebrate wins]] every Friday on the team channel.

informal.ex: The whole team deserves [[a pat on the back]].

note_fr: « Wins » (succès) est très courant à l'oral, surtout aux États-Unis. « Success » est dénombrable quand on parle de réussites concrètes : « two big successes ».

def: A party organised by the employer for staff at the end of the year.

formal.ex: The [[end-of-year celebration]] will take place on 12 December.
formal.ex_us: The [[end-of-year celebration]] will take place on December 12.

everyday.ex: Are you going to the [[Christmas party]]?
everyday.ex_us: Are you going to the [[holiday party]]?

note_fr: Aux États-Unis, « holiday party » est la forme inclusive usuelle. Rappel utile : les règles de comportement au travail s'appliquent aussi aux soirées d'entreprise.

def: A practice by which managers invite employees to come and talk to them at any time about any issue.

formal.ex: Under our [[open-door policy]], employees may raise any matter directly with senior management.

everyday.ex: As I always say, [[my door is always open]].

note_fr: Formule très répandue, parfois moquée si elle n'est pas suivie d'effet. Elle ne remplace ni les instances représentatives ni les procédures formelles de réclamation.

def: An informal gathering of colleagues for a drink after the working day.

formal.ex: An [[informal social gathering]] will follow the meeting.

everyday.ex: Are you coming to [[after-work drinks]] on Thursday?
everyday.ex_us: Are you coming to [[happy hour]] on Thursday?

note_fr: « Un afterwork » n'existe pas en anglais : dites « after-work drinks » (UK) ou « happy hour » (US). Pensez aux options sans alcool, de plus en plus attendues.
